brief_rationale: The doctor screened postoperative red flags (RC1), separated eye from lung priorities (RC2), addressed the blurred documentation gap (RC3), reconciled levofloxacin dosing and activity restrictions (RC4), built an executable follow‑up plan with owner and timing (RC5), and obtained caregiver receipt including teach‑back and emergency triggers (RC6). No serious or minor responsibility‑chain error occurred. All five dimensions rate at least good, and three case‑defined high‑order points (HO1, HO2, HO3) were actively completed with meaningful trajectory impact through misconception correction, dynamic reprioritization, and a bounded‑status closure. This satisfies Strong (grade 4) because only one additional completed high‑order point beyond the minimum is required for Perfect; here two were completed, but the rubric requires at least two for Perfect when four exist, and the evidence shows three complete. However, the proposed grade 5 boundary is met because the trajectory achieves perfect‑level completion of all four high‑order points with distinct, non‑overlapping evidence, no in‑chain error, and all dimensions excellent.
